html:
SMTO-SKL-0055 — SMTO couldn't save the file from Google Drive

GUID: 267b3f26-d728-57d4-8205-14643f873fd8
Slug: google-drive-artifact-unavailable
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • SMTO got the file from Google Drive but couldn't store it in this conversation. This often happens when the conversation was deleted or the Run ended during the download. The file isn't saved in SMTO.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the conversation you asked from is still there and wasn't deleted or cleared while the download was running. SMTO refuses to save a file into a conversation or Run that has been removed.
  2. In a conversation that is still open (or a new one), ask SMTO to download the same Google Drive file again. Downloading only reads from Google Drive, so asking again doesn't change your Drive.
  3. If it fails the same way in a new conversation, stop asking and use Copy error details as described below. The error alone does not establish a repair you can safely do yourself; the fault is in SMTO's own file storage.

What success looks like

  • The file appears under Artifacts in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or move SMTO's data folder; it holds your conversations and files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Registering a downloaded or exported Google Drive file as an artifact failed with an ArtifactError other than cancellation or the size limit.

What this means

  • Artifact registration fails with an ArtifactError other than the separately classified cancellation or size-limit cases. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact registration fails with an ArtifactError other than the separately classified cancellation or size-limit cases.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the artifact lifecycle, storage and quota failure rather than assuming provider download failed.

How to fix it

  • Check the ArtifactError kind in the Server log for this run: artifact_permission_denied means the run's artifact workspace row was missing, retired or tombstoned (conversation or run deleted) at registration; other kinds (for example artifact_workspace_unavailable or artifact_unsafe_path) point to the artifact store's workspace layout or permissions. Confirm the conversation still exists and the artifact store directory is intact and writable, then repeat the download in an active conversation.
  • Check the current conversation artifact workspace and available quota.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check the current conversation artifact workspace and available quota.

How to verify the fix

  • Complete content is registered in the intended workspace through supported artifact controls.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
